Ettool channel setup, check, and reset logic for XDP network devices and bonded slaves.

# Purpose
`ethtool-channels` is a configuration stage for network devices that uses `ethtool` ioctl calls to set and verify RX channel and RSS settings. It runs only when the network provider is `xdp`, and it skips direct device setup when the system uses a network namespace. The stage also checks root permission before it changes device configuration. Its main task is to prepare the interface for either `simple` RSS queue mode or `dedicated` RSS queue mode, based on `config->net.xdp.rss_queue_mode` and `config->layout.net_tile_count`.

The file handles both normal interfaces and bonded interfaces by reading slave devices from `/sys/class/net/.../bonding/slaves` and applying the same settings to each slave. In [`init`](<#init>), it resets RSS hash settings, sets the channel count, clears ntuple rules, and, in dedicated mode, isolates queue 0 and installs UDP destination port rules for Firedancer traffic ports. The [`check`](<#check>) logic verifies that the device state matches the expected channel count, RSS table layout, ntuple feature state, and ntuple rules, and it reports partial or missing configuration when the device state does not match. The [`fini`](<#fini>) logic restores the device to its default state by resetting RSS settings, restoring the maximum channel count, and clearing ntuple rules, while leaving the ntuple feature flag unchanged.
